note.title: Sensor window grouping: project overview
note.summary: A tiny Python repository. window.py defines contains(start, end, sample), which decides whether a dashboard window shows a reading. The window end is inclusive by a recorded decision.
note.body:
Layout: README.md, window.py, test_window.py. No other directories or registered documentation sources were found.

Behavior: contains(start, end, sample) returns start <= sample <= end. Both bounds are inclusive.

Tests: run `python3 -B test_window.py`. It uses unittest. The single test, test_common_positions, checks the start boundary (10), a middle value (15) and a value past the end (21). It does not test the end boundary.

History: PR 7 (merged) changed the end comparison from exclusive (<) to inclusive (<=). Its description says operators compare neighboring sensor windows, and a sample exactly at a shared end must appear in both panels. The overlap is intentional. A maintainer comment in the PR says the inclusive end was accepted for that reason.

Review guidance: do not report the overlap between adjacent windows as a bug without new evidence. This history is a recorded decision, not proof that the current code matches it in every caller; only window.py exists in this repository. The tests do not lock the end-inclusive behavior, so a regression there would go unnoticed.

claims.text: contains(start, end, sample) returns start <= sample <= end, so both bounds are inclusive.
The README says contains decides which dashboard windows show a reading, and that `python3 -B test_window.py` checks basic behavior.
The only test, test_common_positions, checks values 10, 15 and 21 in the window 10 to 20. It has no assertion for sample equal to end.
PR 7 changed the end bound from exclusive to inclusive so that a sample at the shared end of neighboring windows appears in both panels; the overlap is intentional.
Because the tests do not assert the end boundary, a regression to an exclusive end would not fail the current test suite.

Limitation: the PR history is a cached default-diff artifact; its commit linkage, freshness and final merged diff are not verified, and it does not prove the dashboard callers still rely on this behavior.
